data.why: The dashboard ships its own validated grid.geojson for Guwahati (and five more cities under frontend/data/cities/) with no build step; nagpur's grid.geojson is named only as a ready-made file for exercising the page's drag-and-drop 'load your own grid' feature.

goals: Explore the measured land-surface-temperature field across a city's 100 m grid cells
Compare NDVI (vegetation cover) against temperature to see what is driving the heat pattern
Drag a selection box and preview the post-mitigation temperature surface if the recommended interventions were carried out
Review the budget-ranked list of cooling interventions (cooling per rupee) and their costs
Switch between cities (or drop a self-built grid.geojson) to compare a different study area without re-running the pipeline

review.summary: The tree captures what the dashboard is for: finding where a city's surface is hottest, relating it to vegetation, funding interventions by cooling per rupee under a budget, and previewing the cooled surface. All 12 screens I sampled match their nodes. It needs a light pass before filing: regroup t7 and t12, demote the zoom and layer-toggle tasks, add the thermal-surface feature and a provenance-check task, and fix the f1 reference and the note about Cool Roof being excluded in the early screens.
